title: Workday brings autopilots to hiring, payroll in autonomous AI bet
summary: The company said its latest tools will anticipate needs and take actions across finance and HR workflows, with customer-defined controls.

title: Roofer sues after allegedly being told ‘no one pays overtime in construction work’
summary: While it is common for certain salaried workers to be exempt from the FLSA’s overtime requirement, blue-collar workers are nonexempt.

title: SHRM loses service dog trial, owes former job applicant $400K
summary: While SHRM strongly decried the decision and said it was considering an appeal, attorneys for the plaintiff vowed to “vigorously defend” the judgment.

title: ‘Capability anxiety’ may be pulling companies down
summary: Only 30% of the more than 500 employers surveyed by WTW said they’ve established processes for identifying and tracking worker skills.

title: HR leaders feel positive about their outlook, but can’t back it up with numbers
summary: A 2026 report from Betterworks shows a quantitative disconnect between HR’s optimism and demonstrated proof of concept for outcomes, suggesting HR should buckle down on data.

title: Noncompete agreements may not do what they’re supposed to do
summary: A recent study found that including this restriction in a contract not only makes it difficult to hire workers, it also does not prevent information leaks.

title: FedEx worker’s 6 harassment reports not protected by Title VII, 5th Circuit says
summary: The plaintiff’s allegations of bullying, aggressive and passive aggressive behavior don’t automatically rise to the level of discrimination, the court held.

title: Whole Foods defeats bias suit after catching plaintiff faking time records
summary: A federal judge cited the company’s investigation of video recordings in which the worker immediately left the worksite after clocking in to work.

title: Company’s male-only job openings lead to $500K settlement with EEOC
summary: The commission has repeatedly challenged hiring policies that exclude applicants because of their sex and employers that retaliate against HR professionals for hiring women.

title: Women fall through the cracks at work, especially on boards, report says
summary: Continued analysis of gender representation on corporate boards corroborates previous findings on the clock winding back for women at work.
